peopleAlsoAsk.question: How many times can you freeze and thaw AAV?
peopleAlsoAsk.snippet: Don't freeze and thaw multiple times. The titer may drop 2-3 fold (or more) with each freeze-thaw cycle. Therefore, it is best to avoid.

peopleAlsoAsk.question: Does cell lysis occur in the lysogenic cycle?
peopleAlsoAsk.snippet: Temperate phages may choose to infect either through the lytic or the lysogenic cycles1. Whereas the lytic cycle leads to lysis of the bacterial cell, in the lysogenic cycle the phage genome integrates into the bacterial genome, and the lysogenized bacterium becomes immune to further infection by the same phage1.
peopleAlsoAsk.title: Communication between viruses guides lysis-lysogeny decisions

peopleAlsoAsk.question: What is the cycle of viral infection replication and cell destruction called?
peopleAlsoAsk.snippet: The lytic cycle (/ˈlɪtɪk/ LIT-ik) is one of the two cycles of viral reproduction (referring to bacterial viruses or bacteriophages), the other being the lysogenic cycle. The lytic cycle results in the destruction of the infected cell and its membrane.
peopleAlsoAsk.title: Lytic cycle - Wikipedia

peopleAlsoAsk.question: What lytic infection results in the death of the host cell?
peopleAlsoAsk.snippet: Lysis results in the death of an infected host cell, these types of viruses are referred to as cytolytic. An example is variola major also known as smallpox. Enveloped viruses, such as influenza A virus, are typically released from the host cell by budding.
